newsitem.title: GERMANY: Karstadt shares on roll from store project.
newsitem.headline: Karstadt shares on roll from store project.

text.p: Karstadt AG, the German retailer whose shares have been on a rollercoaster ride and dogged by rumours, is back on the uptrend amid views by analysts that a pilot project to revamp stores is taking hold.
Karstadt surged six percent on Wednesday, rising 37.50 marks to 663 and far outpacing a 1.9 percent gain during bourse trading in Germany's 30-share DAX index.

The Essen-based retailer's shares have tacked on an 11 percent gain since last Thursday due to some analyst upgrades and Karstadt executives saying the critical project at a store in Duisburg was generating double-digit sales growth.

"The thinking is that if they span this out across the chain, this could have a profound impact on Karstadt's performance," said William Cullum, European retail analyst at Paribas Capital Markets in London, who recently raised Karstadt from "sell" to "market neutral".
The store's clothing section was remodelled last spring to offer a "theme" approach to replace the old-style department store format increasingly being shunned by consumers.

The pilot project, which costs about 600 marks per square metre in renovation costs, requires far less stock to be kept in stores and has apparently increased customer traffic through better efforts to target consumer interest.
A Karstadt spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday that sales in the store's new clothing section have so far been up about 15 percent on a same-space basis.

A Karstadt store in Duesseldorf will soon be fully remodelled as part of the project that calls for a focus on six key areas that include top-end consumer electronics, luxury accessories, household items, gourmet food and sporting goods.
More details about the project are expected to be discussed at Karstadt's annual general meeting on July 23.

But it will take about two to three years for all of the nearly 230 Karstadt and Hertie department stores to be remodelled amid some criticism that the retailer lags far behind rival Metro AG in catching on to new consumer trends.

"The results so far show that the new concept that Karstadt has developed has a chance of being successful," said Joerg Christians at Trinkaus Capital Management, who rates Karstadt a sell and thinks the share is overvalued.
"I think the restructuring is a major step forward, but you have to remember it will not happen overnight," he said.

Karstadt is in dire need of a makeover since its sales have been in a slump. They fell 2.3 percent in the first quarter to 5.98 billion marks in the first quarter and sales in the first five months of the year fell on a same-store basis.

The recent gains have also come despite growing speculation that Karstadt will be tossed out of the blue-chip DAX index and replaced by up-and-coming sportswear group Adidas AG at a meeting of the German bourse scheduled for July 22.

The market is also picking over rumours that Karstadt may be transformed into a holding group and that its units - department store group Karstadt, mail-order group Neckermann and travel group NUR -- would be listed as individual shares.

Karstadt shares have also whipped around in recent weeks on expectations that German holding group WCM was interested in taking a stake in the retailer. WCM said in late June that it had abandoned interest in buying into Karstadt.
Calls for Karstadt Chief Executive Walter Deuss, in power since 1979, to resign have also caused its shares to waver.
Despite the turbulence, analysts and market dealers said Karstadt shares should find hope from the turnaround strategy.

"Clearly the risk of being taken out of the index is a downside factor," said one dealer. "But people are so desperate to hear restructuring stories from a German company, that the stock price is quickly off to the races."
--Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
